entry.title: Microsoft’s Mustafa Suleyman says its AI outperforms doctors on hard cases as he chases ‘medical superintelligence’
entry.summary: Microsoft’s new AI diagnostic system beat generalist doctors on hard cases, according to a study in Science. But most of the improvement seems to come from the AI models underneath, not from Microsoft’s system itself.

entry.title: Canva releases its first image generation model
entry.summary: Canva is making its new image model available to all users, promising better, more customizable performance at lower costs.

entry.title: OpenAI makes its Jev competitor widely available as decision model competition heats up
entry.summary: OpenAI is launching its decision model to the world. Can it compete with the original Jev?

entry.title: 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password
entry.summary: The new feature allows agents to log into a customer's personal accounts while still protecting the private credentials that secure those accounts.

entry.title: OpenAI working on new $30B raise at $1.25T valuation ahead of IPO
entry.summary: Should OpenAI command an over $1 trillion valuation with this round, it would break records as the most highly valued private company ever.

entry.title: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing
entry.summary: MIT researchers marooned 13 AIs on a virtual island, and they responded by inventing games, mourning a lost ring and, eventually, getting better at their jobs.

entry.title: Uber rival inDrive eyes 2027 robotaxi tests in Central Asia with Pony AI and Nvidia
entry.summary: The company plans to begin testing Pony.ai's robotaxis in Kazakhstan's capital in the first half of 2027.

entry.title: From Toast to Bessemer: Who founders will hear from at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026
entry.summary: Hosted by TechCrunch in partnership with Fidelity Private Shares, the full-day event goes beyond fundraising and AI to explore the realities of finding customers, building teams, sharpening a pitch, developing founder leadership, and scaling companies both inside and outside traditional startup hubs.

entry.title: Hottest toy for Christmas? Nvidia CEO plays with adorable Microduck robots, 20,000 sell
entry.summary: The robots, stomping their little feet and making tiny R2-D2 noises, sat, fell down dead for a "nap," and summersaulted on voice command.

entry.title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing ‘significant risks’
entry.summary: OpenAI will cut frontier models off from the internet weeks after one of its engineers said that solution wouldn't work.

entry.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
entry.summary: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.

entry.title: Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats.
entry.summary: A new study found Grok's AI overwhelmingly recommends Republican candidates while OpenAI's GPT favors Democrats, with the two AI models disagreeing in more than 90% of nearly 500 election races.

entry.summary: The footage looks okay, as long as you're not seeking artistry, inspiration, or human interest.

entry.title: Anthropic officially files for its public debut
entry.summary: Anthropic has officially filed for an IPO, revealing soaring revenue, mounting losses, major enterprise adoption, and an unusual governance structure designed to preserve founder control and its AI safety mission.

entry.title: SpaceX locks in $40B GPU financing deal with Apollo
entry.summary: SpaceX has locked in a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing to pay for AI chips and related data center equipment, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing Monday. In a statement, SpaceX called it the “largest committed GPU financing” ever.

entry.title: Anthropic’s IPO filing reveals its strategy for keeping enterprise customers hooked
entry.summary: Anthropic’s S-1 shows more than half of its $100,000-plus customers now use both the Claude Platform and a first-party app, a cross-selling playbook reminiscent of Amazon that’s making enterprise customers stickier.
